themes_detail.label: Water Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK, a 1100% increase versus the 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a sudden contamination or discoloration event affecting tap water in East Flatbush.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35)
1100% spike represents first major water quality incident in baseline period
Timing suggests acute event rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP to confirm water main breaks, contamination notices, or boil water advisories issued in CD 317 this week
Interview affected residents about water discoloration, odor, or taste changes; cross-check addresses of complainants

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints exploded to 26 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1633% spike versus the 1.5 weekly average over 8 weeks, indicating a coordinated or rapid-onset vandalism surge across the district.
evidence: 26 graffiti complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 16.33, highest severity score)
1633% increase represents single largest spike in dataset
No follow-up data on whether spike has sustained or declined in past week
reporting_angles: Visit the geographic cluster of complaints from 2 weeks ago to assess whether graffiti remains or has been painted over; photograph evidence
Interview NYPD and NYC Parks to determine if gang tagging, organized crews, or vandalism-as-protest pattern identified

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK, a 433% increase versus the 0.8 weekly average over 8 weeks, suggesting localized air pollution, construction emissions, or environmental hazard exposure in East Flatbush.
evidence: 4 air quality complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.91)
433% spike; timing overlaps with 15 DOB building permits filed in district, including 10 alteration projects
No air quality data from NYC DEP or EPA provided; spike warrants independent air monitoring verification
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the addresses of 4 air quality complaints with active DOB permit sites to determine if construction dust, debris burning, or industrial emissions are source
Request NYC DEP air quality monitoring data and EPA AirNow readings for East Flatbush zip codes for past 2 weeks

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 3 THREE WEEKS AGO, a 2300% spike versus the 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks, indicating a disposal or bike-sharing problem emerging in the district.
evidence: 3 abandoned bike complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69)
2300% increase; no clear follow-up data on whether issue has persisted or resolved
No visible bike-share or transportation policy changes noted in news or budget data
reporting_angles: Locate the 3 addresses where abandoned bikes were reported; photograph current condition to assess if bikes remain or have been removed
Contact Citi Bike and NYC Sanitation to determine if reported bikes are abandoned personal property or damaged share-bikes awaiting pickup

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints rose to 6 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 433% increase versus the 1.1 weekly average over 8 weeks, potentially signaling disease, rodent/pest outbreak, or unsanitary conditions accelerating in the district.
evidence: 6 dead animal complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.13)
433% spike; overlaps with elevated unsanitary condition complaints (997 total over 90 days, baseline high)
No current week follow-up data; unclear if spike has sustained or resolved
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Health Dept. and NYPD to determine if elevated dead animals correlate with rat/pest infestation reports, disease surveillance alerts, or rodent control operations
Interview residents at complaint addresses about observable sanitation or pest issues
